metadata.title: Can older workers stay productive? The role of ICT skills and training

extraction.outcome_summary: The study used the Korean sample of PIAAC to examine whether ICT skills and job training were associated with higher hourly wages among full-time workers aged 16–65, with a final analytic sample of 2,620 respondents. Using Mincer-type linear regressions, it found positive returns to ICT skills and job training overall, and the job-training premium was larger for workers aged 50–65 than for younger workers. The interaction models suggested that older workers with higher education or skill-intensive occupations benefited most from ICT skills, with the largest estimated wage gains appearing when ICT skills and training were combined. Missing ICT proficiency scores were handled through regression-based multiple imputation, and robustness checks used numeracy in place of literacy as the ability proxy.
